name: Unveiling the Tricks: Automated Detection of Dark Patterns in Mobile Applications
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces UIGuard, a system that examines mobile UI visuals and text to detect dark patterns, together with a labeled dataset of benign and malicious interfaces.

name: UIClip: A Data-driven Model for Assessing User Interface Design
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: UIClip assesses UI design quality and visual relevance from screenshots and descriptions, using crawled, augmented and human-rated interfaces for training.

name: Inferring Alt-text For UI Icons With Large Language Models During App Development
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. This is a UI accessibility and element-description method; autonomous GUI control is not evaluated.
summary: Introduces IconDesc, which generates mobile icon alt-text from partial UI context such as element identifiers, bounds, nearby text and hierarchy. Model evaluation and a user study examine the resulting accessibility descriptions.

name: UXAgent: An LLM Agent-Based Usability Testing Framework for Web Design
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The system is intended to help researchers refine study designs before conducting studies with human participants.
summary: Introduces UXAgent, which uses simulated users and a browser connector to test website usability and present their actions, responses, and recordings to UX researchers.

name: AgentA/B: Automated and Scalable Web A/BTesting with Interactive LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v4). The abstract describes a controlled shopping-site experiment comparing simulated agents with human behavior.
summary: Introduces AgentA/B, which uses persona-based LLM agents to navigate real webpages and perform shopping interactions for simulated web A/B tests.

name: WebGen-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Generating Interactive and Functional Websites from Scratch
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The benchmark targets website code generation; browser navigation is used to test the generated sites.
summary: Introduces WebGen-Bench for evaluating agents that generate multi-file websites, using a web-navigation agent to check whether the resulting pages pass interaction tests.

name: Do MLLMs Capture How Interfaces Guide User Behavior? A Benchmark for Multimodal UI/UX Design Understanding
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available. This benchmark measures UI/UX design understanding from static image pairs; it does not measure autonomous GUI action execution.
summary: Introduces WiserUI-Bench, pairing real UI variants from industry A/B tests with observed behavioral winners and expert explanations. It evaluates models’ ability to predict the more effective interface and explain its effect on user behavior.

name: Leveraging Vision-Language Models for Visual Grounding and Analysis of Automotive UI
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). Automotive interfaces are the primary setting; ScreenSpot is reported as a separate cross-domain evaluation.
summary: Introduces AutomotiveUI-Bench-4K and a fine-tuned vision-language model for locating elements and evaluating automotive infotainment interfaces.

name: Build the web for agents, not agents for the web
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). This is a position paper proposing interface design principles.
summary: Proposes Agentic Web Interface (AWI), a website interface intended for agent navigation, and sets out six design principles for web-agent use.

name: Machine-Readable Ads: Accessibility and Trust Patterns for AI Web Agents interacting with Online Advertisements
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Compares DOM-based and pixel-based web agents on a cloned news site containing advertisements, consent dialogs and paywalls. The study examines how interface presentation affects ad interaction and consequential subscription choices.

name: WebMMU: A Benchmark for Multimodal Multilingual Website Understanding and Code Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces WebMMU, a multilingual benchmark for website visual question answering, element grounding, code editing, and mockup-to-code generation.

name: WebGen-Agent: Enhancing Interactive Website Generation with Multi-Level Feedback and Step-Level Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUI agents provide testing feedback for generated websites; WebGen-Agent itself generates website code.
summary: Introduces WebGen-Agent for website code generation, using screenshot critiques and GUI-agent tests to refine code and provide step-level training rewards.

name: Understanding User Experiences of Computer Use Agents: Design Space and Opportunities for Building Agent UX Prototypes
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). AgentUXlab prototypes agent experiences for a website and runs them in a browser.
summary: Maps design considerations for computer-use agent experiences and introduces AgentUXlab, a browser-based probe for prototyping and evaluating agent UX on a website.

name: A Multimodal GUI Architecture for Interfacing with LLM-Based Conversational Assistants
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The assistant uses application-exposed tools and navigation semantics.
summary: Presents an MCP architecture that exposes an application's GUI navigation graph and view-specific tools to speech-enabled LLM assistants for voice interaction.

name: SusBench: An Online Benchmark for Evaluating Dark Pattern Susceptibility of Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces SusBench, an online benchmark that inserts dark-pattern designs into consumer websites for agent evaluation. A human study checks the realism of the interventions, and agent trials compare susceptibility across pattern types.

name: Investigating the Impact of Dark Patterns on LLM-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents LiteAgent for recording web-agent interactions and TrickyArena for enabling or disabling dark patterns in controlled websites. Experiments compare how individual patterns, combined patterns and visual or HTML changes affect agent decisions.

name: WebVIA: A Web-based Vision-Language Agentic Framework for Interactive and Verifiable UI-to-Code Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its main objective is UI code generation; the agent explores interface states to support that process.
summary: WebVIA combines a web UI exploration agent, interactive UI-to-Code generation, and validation of generated code's interactivity.

name: Computer-Use Agents as Judges for Generative User Interface
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: AUI-Gym evaluates generated websites by having computer-use agents attempt tasks whose executability is checked programmatically. A feedback dashboard condenses navigation histories into visual summaries that a coding agent can use to revise an interface.

name: DECEPTICON: How Dark Patterns Manipulate Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Its tasks comprise 600 generated and 100 real-world cases.
summary: DECEPTICON is an environment of 700 web navigation tasks that isolates dark patterns to measure how deceptive interface designs steer agent actions.

name: It's a TRAP! Task-Redirecting Agent Persuasion Benchmark for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces TRAP, which evaluates task-redirection attacks embedded in realistic web interfaces. Controlled website clones and a modular injection framework support comparisons of persuasion techniques and contextual changes across agents.

name: FronTalk: Benchmarking Front-End Development as Conversational Code Generation with Multi-Modal Feedback
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). Its main task is front-end code generation; web agents explore generated sites to assess and critique implementations.
summary: FronTalk benchmarks multi-turn front-end code generation from text and visual feedback; a web agent explores generated sites for evaluation and in AceCoder.

name: The Behavioral Fabric of LLM-Powered GUI Agents: Human Values and Interaction Outcomes
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces a controlled web-task testbed for studying how stated preferences and human values influence GUI-agent decisions. It analyzes how personas alter navigation and how prominent interface cues can override the intended preference guidance.

name: How do Visual Attributes Influence Web Agents? A Comprehensive Evaluation of User Interface Design Factors
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces VAF, a controlled pipeline that varies webpage appearance while retaining item semantics. It measures both agent clicks and reasoning references to study which visual design factors change browsing decisions.

name: SimGym: Traffic-Grounded Browser Agents for Offline A/B Testing in E-Commerce
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported validation compares simulated results with human outcomes from UI changes on one major e-commerce platform.
summary: SimGym runs traffic-grounded synthetic buyers as browser agents to compare e-commerce storefront variants offline, using buyer profiles derived from production interactions.

name: Mapping the Design Space of User Experience for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Develops a taxonomy of computer-use-agent interaction design through system review and practitioner interviews. A Wizard-of-Oz study then examines how users respond to normal, erroneous, and risky web-based execution, focusing on control, explanation, prompts, and mental models.

name: Terminal Is All You Need: Design Properties for Human-AI Agent Collaboration
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent conceptual HCI work about agent-facing interfaces; the abstract does not report GUI task experiments or a new evaluated CUA.
summary: This position paper derives interface design principles from terminal-based human-agent collaboration: representational compatibility, transparent actions and low participation barriers. It argues that graphical and other agent-facing modalities should provide these properties explicitly.

name: IntentWeave: A Progressive Entry Ladder for Multi-Surface Browser Agents in Cloud Portals
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The prototype and user study are set on a single cloud website.
summary: Introduces IntentWeave, a design space and browser-extension prototype for placing web-agent assistance across browser surfaces, evaluated through a study of three entry strategies.

name: Vision2Web: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Visual Website Development with Agent Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The benchmark evaluates website development by coding agents, with a GUI agent used for verification.
summary: Introduces Vision2Web, a benchmark for website development from images, spanning UI-to-code, multi-page frontend and full-stack tasks, with a GUI agent verifier and VLM-based judge.

name: "What Did It Actually Do?": Understanding Risk Awareness and Traceability for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Presents an interview study of computer-use agent risks and AgentTrace, a prototype interface showing agent actions, resource access, permission history, and lasting changes.

name: MAESTRO: Adapting GUIs and Guiding Navigation with User Preferences in Conversational Agents with GUIs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces MAESTRO, a conversational GUI system that remembers user preferences, adapts interface options, and guides backtracking in multistep booking decisions.

name: Avenir-UX: Automated UX Evaluation via Simulated Human Web Interaction with GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Avenir-UX combines grounded web interaction with simulated user profiles and structured usability measures to produce evaluations of website journeys. The paper describes its architecture and use of SUS, step-wise ease questions and think-aloud traces for automated UX reporting.

name: Beyond Chat and Clicks: GUI Agents for In-Situ Assistance via Live Interface Transformation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: DOMSteer translates help requests and live page context into reversible DOM changes such as control highlighting, contextual tooltips and layout reorganization. The work evaluates in-place GUI assistance with interface tests, use cases and a comparative user study.

name: PlayCoder: Making LLM-Generated GUI Code Playable
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: PlayEval measures whether generated GUI applications remain logically playable, using PlayTester to execute task-oriented GUI playthroughs. PlayCoder closes the loop between repository-aware generation, interactive testing and targeted code repair.

name: AgentLens: Adaptive Visual Modalities for Human-Agent Interaction in Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). Its reported user findings come from a controlled study with 21 participants.
summary: Introduces AgentLens, a mobile GUI agent that shows full, partial, or generated interface views during background task execution to support user interaction.

name: Training Computer Use Agents to Assess the Usability of Graphical User Interfaces
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: uxCUA learns to assess interface usability by choosing interaction flows, executing them and predicting a numerical usability score. Training uses interactive UIs with usability labels and human preferences, with evaluations on synthetic and real interfaces.

name: Beyond Screenshots: Evaluating VLMs' Understanding of UI Animations
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AniMINT evaluates how VLMs perceive, explain and interpret UI animations using densely annotated videos. The study distinguishes basic motion recognition from higher-level animation meaning and probes motion, context and perceptual cues.

name: Augmenting Interface Usability Heuristics for Reliable Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The agent results come from controlled UI-Verse environments.
summary: A study adapts interface usability heuristics for computer-use agents and evaluates augmented designs in UI-Verse, a suite of controlled interface environments.

name: VISTA: An End-to-End Benchmark for Visual Spec-to-Web-App Coding Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent GUI-application generation benchmark with real component interaction probes; its main evaluated agents are application coders, not general GUI task executors.
summary: VISTA evaluates coding agents that turn design handoffs into working web and Android applications. Its evaluator locates annotated interactive components and probes their behavior, keeping visual localization distinct from functional correctness.

name: PerceptUI: LLM Agents as Human-Aligned Synthetic Users for UI/UX Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces PerceptUI, a persona-conditioned model for predicting how particular users answer questions about interfaces, supporting synthetic UI/UX evaluation.

name: Reasoning for Mobile User Experience with Multimodal LLMs: Task, Benchmark, and Approach
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces UXBench for diagnosing usability issues from UI screenshots and UI-UX, a reinforcement-trained model for reasoning about those interface problems.

name: AOHP: An Open-Source OS-Level Agent Harness for Personalized, Efficient and Secure Interaction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported task-completion, token-cost, and security-policy results come from preliminary experiments.
summary: Introduces AOHP, an Android OS-level harness that treats agents as system actors and provides adaptive interfaces, agent interfaces, and information-flow controls.

name: Designing Agent-Ready Websites for AI Web Agents: A Framework for Machine Readability, Actionability, and Decision Reliability
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The comparison uses two versions of one website prototype in a controlled experiment.
summary: Proposes an agent-ready website design framework for e-commerce browser agents and compares it with a human-oriented site on shopping tasks, outcomes, steps, and token use.

name: WebGrader: Training LLMs for Web Development with Self-Evolving Programmatic Grader
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces WebGrader, a programmatic grader for website generation that plans interaction flows, runs them in a live browser, and uses observed outcomes as RL rewards.

name: From Blind Edits to Verified Repair: Building Trustworthy User-Side LLM Agents for Web Accessibility
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Builds a local browser-extension agent that generates and verifies additive CSS repairs for WCAG web accessibility violations.

name: Affora: A Design System for Agent-Friendly Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The workflow case offers preliminary evidence of lower interaction cost.
summary: Presents Affora, a design system with reusable components and executable checks for interfaces used by computer-use agents, informed by studies of components and visual variation.

name: A Dual-Process Perspective on Nudge Susceptibility in LLM-Based GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies how automatic defaults and reflective social-influence cues affect GUI-agent shopping decisions under different reasoning configurations. A randomized simulated-shopping experiment finds that reasoning changes the type of susceptibility rather than uniformly removing interface influence.

document.reason: Document declaration only. The paper does not establish code, model-weight or underlying dataset permissions through this license.

document.basis: The exact-v1 arXiv HTML infobox (#license-tr) declares License: CC BY 4.0 for this paper document.

name: OpenVAM: Open-World Visual Attention Modeling with VLMs
notes: Static human-attention modeling on U-EYE webpage screenshots, with FIWI held out from training; no live-browser, agent-action or task-success evaluation. Gemini-generated reference rationales are expert-checked, and JScore compares generated text with references; human validation covers a separate 100-image subset. Reference text and heatmap alignment do not establish causal explanations of gaze or temporal scanpaths. Several baseline scores come from prior papers.
summary: Combines dense saliency prediction with explanations of attended elements, including webpage layouts; evaluates human-attention agreement and textual rationales rather than agent actions.

name: WebUIProof: Benchmarking WebUI Code Generators with UI-Agent Execution Harness
notes: Adjacent evaluation infrastructure: the target is generated WebUI functionality, not a general score for computer-use agents. This annotation is based on the complete retained abstract.
summary: Introduces an execution-based benchmark for generated web interfaces, with a headless-browser UI-agent harness that checks DOM interactions and functional assertions.

name: A Decade in a Day: Synthesizing Agent-Native Interfaces from Human-Oriented Software Evolution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports studies across releases of six desktop applications and an expanded evaluation across eight applications.
summary: Introduces DeskIF-Bench to study how desktop application interfaces affect agents, and ANIS to synthesize interfaces from installed application capabilities.

name: InterWebCoder: Learning Interactive Webpage Generation from Executable Tests via Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The generated artifact is webpage code; GUI agents appear as a verification baseline.
summary: InterWebCoder trains models to generate interactive webpage code using recorded interactions, executable tests and repair feedback, an adjacent web interface task.

name: Co-Design Bench: Multimodal Collaborative Coding Evaluation for Agentic Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Co-Design Bench to evaluate coding agents that revise applications from multimodal user requests, including UI changes assessed with browser evidence.

name: UI-UG 2: Advancing Mobile UI Understanding and Generation with Fine-Grained Supervision and Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces UI-UG 2, a mobile UI model trained for component understanding, GUI grounding, and structured interface generation with render-aware RL.

name: Interface Quilt: Modifying Applications with Computer Use Agents and Generative UI
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Interface Quilt, which uses computer-use agents and generated UI overlays to modify how existing applications look and behave without source access.

dataset_profile.notes: Publisher-reported current release, separate from the smaller original-paper population. Screenshot pixels are obtained through referenced RICO IDs.

name: UICrit
notes: The published CSV contains critique text, normalized boxes, ratings and RICO IDs; screenshots are referenced through RICO. The README explicitly licenses the work CC-BY-4.0. Its current 1,000-screen, 11,344-critique release differs from the original paper population. The README cites an ACM DOI rather than an arXiv ID, so no paper relation is asserted here. Its README establishes mobile interfaces without naming an operating system.
summary: Mobile-interface critiques and quality ratings with region coordinates and RICO screen references, including a larger three-annotator release than the original paper dataset.

actions: harness-defined browser actions through the task's local browser service

counts.population: hidden test cases summed over the docs/tasks.md table

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Hidden test cases per task. A case passes when its functional checks pass and every visual checkpoint's flat-baseline-normalized RGB SSIM reaches 0.99. A task's reward is passed cases divided by cases, weighted equally.
focus: full-stack website reconstruction from browser exploration, without the source code
visual appearance and functional behavior of the rebuilt site
benchmark_protocol.notes: Agents run through selectable Harbor agents, so observations and actions depend on the agent. Each task requests 8 CPUs, 8 GiB of memory and 20 GiB of disk per environment, with up to 16 hours for the agent.

code.basis: repository LICENSE header; not a weights/data license

name: WebsiteBench
notes: Read at commit 78f5558e. The README and docs/tasks.md were reviewed; the 70 tasks and 46,916 hidden cases were checked by summing the docs/tasks.md table. The README's paper badge has no link and the project page says the paper is coming soon, so no paper relation is recorded. Apache-2.0 is the README's statement for benchmark code, task definitions and verifier. Leaderboard scores were not checked. Nothing was installed or run.
summary: Website reconstruction benchmark: agents explore a production-level site through a browser, rebuild a full-stack version, and are scored by hidden functional and visual test cases across 70 tasks.

name: Rico: A Mobile App Dataset for Building Data-Driven Design Applications
notes: The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. The paper is a distinct resource from the already cataloged Rico dataset (url:0b134b082a7bd507fc6a). The publisher PDF describes 9.7k apps and 72k screens; the project page describes 9.3k apps and 66k screens. The annotation intentionally supplies no merged size claim.
summary: Introduces Rico, collecting Android interface designs and interaction traces through crowdsourced use followed by automated exploration. The paper demonstrates UI-layout retrieval using learned representations and describes visual, textual, structural, and interaction data.
